brief.headline: Push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc (market fair-band floor) and shorten payment to 15 days to free up ₹2.60 L cash, backed by five credible alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price move toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc on the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking prices for this cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 if we commit volume or relax a spec. That's where we want to land.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Shortening payment by 15 days frees up ₹2.60 L of our cash — money we can put to work elsewhere.

brief.financialLeverage: Bprex publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we lean on our own data and on lining up a second source. Our ₹63.21 L annual spend is real money, and we have five strong alternates queued — three listed packaging firms and two large private converters. With no visibility into their balance sheet, we keep the asks firm but fair: price to the market floor and faster payment to help our own cash, while we qualify a backup to reduce dependency.

evidence.point: Market asking price for the 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume.
Cutting payment terms by 15 days frees up cash for us.
We spend this much annually with Bprex.
HDPE resin import unit value stands at this level, giving a raw-material benchmark.
Manjushree Technopack, India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, is a top second-source candidate with strong health and scale.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, B health score 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate, though still a lead to qualify before we RFQ.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable; a robust alternate for bottles and closures, but a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ).

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed firm with broad moulded and blow-moulded packaging capability across bottles and caps — a lead to qualify before we price.

risks: Bprex's financials aren't public, so we can't gauge how healthy or cash-tight they are — keep the push fair and watch for any supply hiccup.

The market-backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are unqualified web finds — useful for negotiation pressure but not yet approved sources; flag any as 'lead to verify' if you name one.
Shortening payment by 15 days helps our cash but may squeeze a supplier whose finances we can't see — pair the ask with a volume commitment or longer contract to soften the blow.

We have no internal price benchmark (no avgPrice or bestPrice data) for rigid plastic packaging, so the market ask is our only anchor — make sure the spec and MOQ match before you lock the ₹0.65–0.80 target.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about moving our 28 mm cap price toward the ₹0.65–0.80 market band and shortening payment to 15 days — we're also qualifying Manjushree and Mold-Tek as second sources, so let's see where we can land together.
